{
  "need": "Belonging",
  "secondary": { "name": "Status", "note": "A new kid who sits apart is also asking: do I matter here, or am I invisible?" },
  "read": "Joining mid-year means all the social maps are already drawn. This student likely feels like an outsider who does not know the rules yet, and sitting apart may be self-protection — if you do not try, you cannot be rejected. Underneath the distance is probably a real wish to connect, blocked by not knowing how to break in.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Leave them alone and give it time — but that quietly signals nobody here is working to include you, which deepens the isolation rather than healing it." },
  "mentorMove": "Hold the expectation that everyone participates and belongs in this room, while actively building a small on-ramp for this student rather than waiting for belonging to happen by accident.",
  "holdFirm": ["Every student is a full member of this class, not a guest waiting to be invited.", "Pair and group work is not optional — it is part of how we learn here."],
  "stayFlexible": ["Let the student choose which group or which partner first, so they have some control over the approach.", "Start with a low-stakes task — a two-minute partner share — before putting them in a larger group spotlight."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 1, "label": "Empathy" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I have been meaning to catch you for two seconds. Starting mid-year is genuinely hard — the class already has its rhythms and you are finding your footing. I see that." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "What has it felt like in here so far? Anything that has made it easier, or anything that is still awkward?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I want to do. I am going to put you with Maya and Darius for the next activity — they are solid and easy to work with. I will frame it so it is a fresh start for the whole group, not a spotlight on you. Does that feel workable, or is there someone else you have had even a little bit of a connection with?" },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding you to being part of this class because my standard is that everyone belongs here and contributes — and I genuinely think you have things to add that this room has not heard yet. This is me saying I am not going to let you disappear into the back." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Over the next few weeks, find one moment to publicly credit this student for a contribution — a good question, a sharp observation — so the class sees them as someone worth knowing. Belonging that sticks is built on status moments, not just proximity."
}
situation: A student who joined mid-year sits apart and has not connected with anyone.
